references.text: The same prohibition against bribes is repeated in Deuteronomy, with similar wording that bribes blind the wise and pervert the cause of the righteous.
A curse is pronounced on anyone who takes a bribe to kill an innocent person, showing the seriousness of accepting bribes.
Proverbs describes how the wicked accept bribes in secret to twist the course of justice.
Whoever seeks profit destroys their own house, but whoever hates bribes will live.
Isaiah condemns leaders who love bribes and chase after gifts, and who do not help the fatherless and widows.
Woe to those who acquit the guilty for a bribe and deprive the innocent of justice.
The Preacher warns that bribes destroy the heart and turn the wise into fools.
Micah condemns leaders who judge for bribes, and priests who teach for payment.
Samuel's sons accepted bribes and twisted justice, unlike their father.
Job describes how fire consumes the tents of those who take bribes.
A thematic parallel illustrating how partiality (which bribes create) distorts the cause of justice.
